narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Annotated Poster"**

The site reads as a printed object: a Bauhaus poster on warm chalk paper, with flat fields of cobalt, vermilion and ochre, solid ink rules, near-square corners, and a geometric motif that recurs from the homepage hero to every post cover and OG card. Over that sits a scholar's annotation layer. Margin notes, mono metadata and captions in a typewriter face carry the caveats, sources and asides a physician-engineer writes in. The poster supplies the colour and the confidence. The annotations supply the voice.

Colour is spent where it carries meaning: category identity, the cover compositions, the hero motif, link and focus details. Everything else is quiet and typographic. Components barely exist as objects. Mono labels, hairlines and 1.5px ink rules do the structural work, so prose and covers lead. Spacing is generous on purpose. The site is airy, never terminal-dense, and readable by people who aren't developers.

Confirmed rejections: the cream + high-contrast serif + terracotta "AI design" default (the cobalt lead is the escape from it), terminal or broadsheet density, loud filled category pills, and going quieter overall. Review said the system could take slightly *more* colour, never less.
keyCharacteristics: Warm chalk ground, warm near-black ink, three Bauhaus primaries with cobalt dominant.
Three faces, three jobs: grotesque display, serif reading, mono annotation. All Greek-capable.
Flat. Depth comes from ink rules and colour fields, not shadows.
Near-square 2px corners: a printed object, not an app card.
Sidenotes are the single signature device. Boldness is spent there and in the covers.

rules.name: The Colour-Is-Category Rule
rules.body: Each primary owns one category: project = cobalt, guide = ochre, opinion = vermilion, personal = ink. A category shows up as a 0.62em colour square beside a mono label, and as the dominant field of its cover. It never appears as a filled pill. Four categories is the cap because there are only so many colours. Anything finer is an uncoloured tag.

rules.name: The Deep-for-Small Rule
rules.body: Accent-coloured text below large sizes uses the `-deep` variant. Paper-coloured text never sits on a vermilion fill at small sizes (4.05:1 fails AA).

rules.name: The Three-Places Rule
rules.body: A palette change touches `tokens.css`, `palette.ts`, and this file. Photo covers and OG cards can't read CSS vars and will drift otherwise.

rules.name: The Greek-or-Nothing Rule
rules.body: Every face must ship a verified Greek subset, checked in font metadata and not in marketing copy. In OG rendering, Latin and Greek register under distinct family names (`Commissioner` / `CommissionerGreek`) with a fallback list. A face without Greek is out, however good it looks.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Annotation Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono marks the annotation layer (metadata, notes, captions, labels) and code. It never sets headings or running prose. Its real italic is loaded, so emphasis inside a note is never a slanted roman.

rules.name: The Curly-Quotes Rule
rules.body: Titles and deks pass through `typeset()` (`src/lib/posts.ts`) wherever they render: page, card, `<title>`, OG card. Frontmatter skips smartypants and a CMS textbox types straight quotes, so this is never left to the author.

rules.name: The Ink-Rule Rule
rules.body: Separation is a line, not a lift. Strong structure gets `1.5px solid ink`, and quiet structure gets a `1px` hairline. Never add a drop shadow to a card, cover or panel.

dos: Do route every colour through a token, and update `tokens.css`, `palette.ts` and this file together.
Do use the `-deep` accent for any small accent-coloured text (The Deep-for-Small Rule).
Do separate with ink rules (1.5px) or hairlines (1px) at a 2px radius (The Ink-Rule Rule).
Do keep mono for the annotation layer (metadata, notes, captions, labels) and code.
Do author sidenotes inline, inside a paragraph, so they have something to anchor to.
Do give every post a cover. `generated` is the default, and photos go through the duotone so they stay siblings.
Do keep generous spacing (`space-5`/`space-6` between sections). Airy is the brief.
donts: Don't drift toward cream + high-contrast serif + terracotta. Cobalt leads.
Don't make the site quieter overall. If anything it can take a little more colour.
Don't use filled, loud category pills. Category is a small square plus a label, and the cover carries the colour.
Don't add drop shadows, rounded app cards or radii above 2px.
Don't introduce a typeface without a verified Greek subset.
Don't set paper-coloured small text on vermilion.
Don't pack the layout to terminal or broadsheet density. Non-developers read this site.
